script: I refused to attend my sister's wedding—my family is stunned.. I was the annoying little sister—always on the brink of being the joke, but secretly worshipping my older bro. We didn't vibe as kids, but at 14 and 17, after her breakup, we hit it off. We kept in touch, she went to uni, I'd drop by, calls, texts, the whole "bestie" thing. She graduated at 23, I was 20, and she jumped abroad to teach. We were still tight, but distance drifts even the best. Fast forward a few years. She met a guy overseas, they moved back to Canada, but she set up in BC while our family stayed in Ontario. Covid hit, they eloped secretly—she'd always wanted a real wedding, but had to keep him in the country. I was like, "Yass, love!" and genuinely happy. Then the pregnancy drama. She visits, tells us she's pregnant. I am pregnant too, and I tell her—thinking she'd be thrilled. She thinks I stole the moment, keeps that beef for the whole pregnancy. She tells Mom I shouldn't even be having a kid, says my mother should have been there when we were born instead of her. Our kids are a week apart, my baby's dad is a ghost, she had my dad and his wife come to stay, my mom can't afford it. She moves back to Ontario after our kids are born, but a month later she bounces back to her husband's country. I am devastated, but I respect her call. We barely talk now, yet I still see us as the besties we were in high school. 2024, I meet an amazing guy. By year's end he says he'll propose in 2025. I tell my sister in January, "save up, babe, this is going to cost a fortune." She's like, "cool, good luck." In August she announces a real wedding in 2027. I am like, "oh wow, congrats!" but it's weird timing because I am planning mine. October, my guy pops the question, we plan a wedding for 2026. Surprise pregnancy throws it to 2027, two months after her big day. I want my niece to be flower girl, but she says she won't be coming, maybe not my brother‑in‑law or nephew either because of cost. I am hurt, but I accept, knowing airfare is a lot. Then comes Christmas: she flies her whole crew to Ontario, wants to spend the holidays with us. She's making double what I do, takes trips to fancy hotels, flies helicopters for wedding pics in BC, the cheapest room is $350. Going alone would cost me $4k. I tell her I'd bring my son, maybe just me if it hurts the wallet. She flips, "you've got to bring both kids, it's her wedding, you owe it." She drops that if I don't bring my youngest she won't know when she'll meet her, because she doesn't know when she'll be in Ontario next. I say I'll be there when I get married, and she says she's not even going to mine because of the cost. She expects me to bring the whole family when I earn half her salary, to a second marriage she's already in, but she's not even coming to my wedding. I've been saving since January 2025, she's jetting around the world, paying for my mom to visit her, but she doesn't seem to care about my special day. I am hurt, resentful. My partner and family think I should go; should she not? Am I being a jerk for not going? Am I overreacting? I am tired of my sister's moments being pushed aside, my birth and wedding being sidelined. What do you all think?
